header: Date: 2026-03-07 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Redwood (Daniel, Maya, Rahul) + Aspen Tech (Elena, Marco, Priya, Tommy)
summary: Introductory onramp to align stakeholders on security, networking, success criteria and pilot runway. Agreed pilot window, deliverables, and specific compliance questions to be answered. Action items assigned for runbook, benchmarking, and scheduling.
topics: Network & VPC options (private deployment vs hosted)
transcript:
[00:00] Daniel Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Daniel with Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, quick intro from us.
[00:08] Elena Ruiz: Hi all, Elena here, lead MLOps at Aspen Tech. We've got Marco, Priya and Tommy on as well.
[00:14] Marco Alvarez: Hey, Marco, platform eng.
[00:17] Priya Nambiar: Priya, security.
[00:19] Tommy Lee: Tommy, product.
[00:21] Daniel Park: Great. Maya and Rahul from our side are here too - Maya's CSM and Rahul's the solutions engineer. We wanted to run through the onramp, align on governance and make sure we capture the compliance bits early.
[00:35] Rahul Sharma: Quick note — we'll cover the runtime options: hosted API, dedicated capacity and private VPC/on-prem. We'll talk tradeoffs: latency, cost, and auditability.
[00:44] Elena Ruiz: That's exactly what we need. Our primary concerns are data residency and KMS integration. We need to know if Redwood can support our HSM or bring-your-own KMS.
[00:56] Rahul Sharma: Yes. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS; for hosted we typically provide managed keys but we can do a dedicated customer KMS integration for enterprise. There might be some additional compliance steps.
[01:12] Priya Nambiar: Are you SOC 2 certified? And do you have ISO or other attestation docs we can share with our auditors?
[01:20] Maya Li: Short answer: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II; we can share our compliance pack. For ISO it's in progress — we have some documentation we can provide. I'll drop the security binder.
[01:30] Tommy Lee: On the network side, Marco was asking whether we should go VPC peering or PrivateLink into a dedicated pool.
[01:38] Marco Alvarez: Yeah, we have strict egress rules, so direct VPC option is preferred, on-prem maybe later. What's the latency delta if we choose private vs hosted?
[01:48] Rahul Sharma: Good question. Hosted API typically hits our multi-tenant endpoint — latency numbers depend on model size and region; Dedicated or Private on your VPC will reduce hop counts and give more consistent latencies. We'll run a small benchmark with your sample prompts and org network.
[02:03] Elena Ruiz: Sounds good. Also, for the pilot we're thinking 2 weeks with a small set of prompts and traffic shaped to our expected production qps.
[02:12] Daniel Park: That's reasonable. What's your target latency P95 and cost envelope?
[02:17] Tommy Lee: We aim for P95 under 400ms for short chat flows, and cost should be within X per 1k tokens — (note: they didn't give exact price here)
[02:28] Maya Li: We'll map cost vs latency across model families and quantization settings. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization to hit your cost targets with an SLO tradeoff.
[02:40] Priya Nambiar: On data retention: we cannot send any PII to a multi-tenant endpoint unless it's encrypted and we have audit trails. Is there per-request redaction or prefix caching concerns?
[02:53] Rahul Sharma: We have prefix/KV caching but it can be disabled per route; audit logs are available and can be pushed to your SIEM. For anything sensitive we recommend private deployment or tokenization before sending.
[03:06] Marco Alvarez: If we do private deployment, how disruptive is the onboarding? What's the typical runway?
[03:12] Maya Li: For a Private VPC onboarding, typical ramp is 3–6 weeks: initial setup, network handshakes, KMS integration, and then pilot. Hosted can be minutes to hours for basic tests. We'll align on a plan.
[03:24] Elena Ruiz: Can you share a runbook with a checklist for each step?
[03:28] Daniel Park: Absolutely — I'll share an onboarding runbook with the access matrix, runbook steps, and required artifacts.
[03:34] [00:34] Rahul Sharma: (typo in generated note) — we also have automated fallback policies to route to cheaper models if capacity constrained, that might help cost.
[03:45] Tommy Lee: Who should own the pilot? Product or platform?
[03:48] Elena Ruiz: I think platform will own infra and product will own success criteria, but MLOps (me) will coordinate.
[03:55] Daniel Park: Good, we'll capture that in the runbook. Next — stakeholders and approvals. Who needs final sign-off for production?
[04:02] Priya Nambiar: Security signs off, then infra ops, and finally product leadership.
[04:07] Marco Alvarez: We'll need a short Risk Assessment doc for our change board.
[04:10] Maya Li: We can provide a template for the Risk Assessment and a network checklist.
[04:15] [05:12] (background cross talk)
[05:20] Rahul Sharma: Let's talk through the pilot measurement plan — we'll collect latency, token cost, error rates, and any hallucination/quality metrics. Do you have existing prompt eval sets?
[05:32] Elena Ruiz: We have a small set of 80 canonical prompts and a heavier set of 1k for broader testing. We'll share the canonical set first.
[05:40] Rahul Sharma: Perfect. We'll run baseline numbers on your prompts vs a few model profiles. We'll capture P50/P95 and token counts.
[05:49] Tommy Lee: Is there tooling in the Console for per-route cost breakdowns?
[05:53] Maya Li: Yes, Console shows per-route model usage, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks. We can grant you access to a demo account so you can see metrics.
[06:03] Priya Nambiar: Demo account — will that contain sample data or our real data?
[06:07] Daniel Park: Demo account will have synthetic/sample data. For your real run we'll set up a staging project with obfuscated data or your private VPC.
[06:16] [08:02] Marco Alvarez: For the KMS integration, do you have a supported list? We use HashiCorp Vault — can Redwood integrate?
[08:10] Rahul Sharma: We integrate with common KMS vendors and have a Vault connector pattern; we'll validate with our infra team.
[08:17] Elena Ruiz: Awesome. Also curious about rollouts — can we do canary and automatic fallback to a smaller model if errors spike?
[08:25] Rahul Sharma: Yes, our rollout policies support canary percentages, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin versions and set thresholds for automatic rollback.
[08:35] Tommy Lee: About observability — do you provide tracing hooks or an API to pull logs into our ELK/Splunk?
[08:42] Maya Li: We provide webhook/export to SIEMs and log push; trace hooks are instrumented in the Console.
[08:48] Priya Nambiar: Do you keep raw request payloads in logs? That's a hard no for us unless encrypted.
[08:54] Rahul Sharma: By default we log metadata and token-level metrics; raw full payloads are not retained unless you enable debug traces, and those can be configured to be retained to your S3 or forwarded to your SIEM under your control.
[09:06] [10:18] Elena Ruiz: Can we get a SLAs doc for uptime and latency? We want to understand the different SLAs for Hosted vs Dedicated.
[10:25] Daniel Park: Yes, Dedicated has an SLA-backed latency and uptime target; hosted is best-effort with usage tiers. We'll share a matrix in the runbook.
[10:33] Marco Alvarez: Pricing ask — we'll need a ballpark for Dedicated baseline commit vs pay-as-you-go hosted.
[10:39] Daniel Park: I'll include ballpark pricing ranges in the follow-up. Exact pricing depends on model families and commit size.
[10:45] [12:01] Priya Nambiar: Audit logs — retention windows and export formats?
[12:06] Maya Li: Audit logs can be retained per contract and exported as JSON lines to your bucket. We also provide access logs and admin actions logs.
[12:14] Tommy Lee: For the pilot scope, let's define success criteria: 95th latency under 400ms for canonical prompts, cost under target X, and no P0 security blockers.
[12:25] Elena Ruiz: Agreed. Also need to validate model quality — we'll run an eval harness.
[12:30] Rahul Sharma: We'll help set up the eval harness and run a baseline.
[12:36] [15:02] (brief pause)
[15:08] Daniel Park: Alright, timeline recap — action items: I'll send runbook, Maya will schedule pilot kickoff, Rahul will run benchmark checklist, and Elena/Priya will confirm compliance list. Pilot tentatively scheduled for week of 2026-03-16.
[15:23] Marco Alvarez: That works. Onboarding access — who needs what? We'll need at least one admin, one read-only, and one dev role.
[15:31] Maya Li: We'll provide role templates and an access matrix.
[15:34] Priya Nambiar: SSO — we use SAML with SCIM user provisioning. Can you support that?
[15:40] Rahul Sharma: Yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. We'll have the integration notes in the runbook.
[15:46] Elena Ruiz: Perfect. For network firewall rules, do you publish IP ranges?
[15:50] Daniel Park: We'll send publishing IP ranges and recommended firewall ports, plus the PrivateLink details if you go that route.
[15:57] [20:02] (side conversation about internal scheduling)
[20:20] Tommy Lee: One more question — if we need on-prem later, what's the upgrade path?
[20:25] Rahul Sharma: We support an on-prem packaged option; migration is a staged process: initial staging in VPC -> private host -> on-prem image. We'll provide the migration playbook.
[20:35] Priya Nambiar: Any customer references with similar compliance needs?
[20:40] Maya Li: We can introduce you to a couple of customers in RegTech and Healthcare that went private deployment.
[20:45] Elena Ruiz: Good.
[20:47] [30:01] (background typing)
[30:15] Daniel Park: Ok wrapping up, any blockers now?
[30:18] Priya Nambiar: Biggest blocker is getting the KMS/Vault connector validated and a clear audit trail for raw payloads.
[30:26] Rahul Sharma: We'll prioritize validating Vault and confirm the audit log export behavior.
[30:32] Marco Alvarez: I'll also need the network checklist to share with the infra team.
[30:37] Daniel Park: We'll include that in the runbook.
[30:40] Elena Ruiz: Timeline — security signoff usually takes our team 5 business days after we receive the docs. So if we get the runbook by Tuesday, we can aim for pilot start on 3/16.
[30:52] Maya Li: Noted. We'll get docs out early week.
[30:56] [40:01] (meeting quiet for a sec)
[40:12] Tommy Lee: Anything else?
[40:14] Daniel Park: No, just to confirm next steps and owners which we've captured. We'll send meeting notes and the runbook link.
[40:22] Elena Ruiz: Thanks everyone.
[40:24] Maya Li: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[40:28] Rahul Sharma: Thanks.
[40:30] [51:48] (meeting ended)

Notes on transcription: occasional overlaps and mis-heard acronyms; some product names may be transcribed imperfectly (e.g., KV cache as 'KV cash', PrivateLink as 'private link').
